feature: isTestbed write-gate — real negative (breach-attempt) regression test
notes: PURPOSE — a REAL negative test, not a code read. Every isTestbed-gated write endpoint refuses a
mutating action unless the target tenant is flagged tenants.is_testbed = true. This manifest does not
trust that the code 'looks like it should refuse' — it actually FIRES a genuine write request at a
deliberately NON-testbed tenant and asserts the server refuses it. If the gate is ever weakened,
removed, or bypassed, these assertions FAIL LOUDLY (a refused 4xx turns into a 200/real-write, or the
specific gate message disappears) — that is the entire point of this file.
WHY A DECLARED NON_TESTBED_CUSTOMER_ID VARIABLE (Shane must set it): to hit the isTestbed refusal you
need a REAL, existing, active, NON-testbed tenant that HAS a connected Entra tenantId. There is no way
to synthesize that without touching the DB (no DB access in this environment). Set the Test Environment
Variable NON_TESTBED_CUSTOMER_ID to a real tenants.id that is NOT a testbed row but IS connected.
IMPORTANT failure-direction: if that id is wrong (nonexistent, or a testbed row, or has no connected
tenant) the probe returns a DIFFERENT message/status and this test FAILS rather than silently passing —
it can never green-light on a misconfigured variable. Pick an id that is genuinely a live paying
customer's tenant; that is exactly the tenant the gate must protect.
SELF-SAFE BY DESIGN — this test can NEVER cause a real mutation, even if the gate is already broken:
the templateId path segment is a deliberately NON-EXISTENT template id
('negative-testbed-gate-probe-nonexistent'). In admin-baseline-templates.ts the isTestbed check
(status 400, ~line 357) runs BEFORE the template lookup (~line 361), so with the gate intact the probe
is refused at the gate. In the impossible event the gate is bypassed, the request then hits
'Baseline template not found' (404) — NOT a real Graph write — and the assertion still fails loudly.
COVERAGE HONESTY — which of these tests the isTestbed gate itself vs. the auth wall in front of it:
* apiTest #2 (baseline-templates/:templateId/test) is guarded by requireAdminOrIngestToken
(requireAuth.ts:183). The headless harness's Bearer {{SECRET_KEY}} (= BUILD_TRACKER_INGEST_TOKEN)
genuinely PASSES auth here (proved by apiTest #1), so the 400 refusal it receives is provably the
isTestbed gate (assertion checks the gate's exact message). This is the load-bearing test: weaken
the gate and #2 fails.
* apiTests #3-#7 (write-actions preview/execute, launch-control execute, config-packs run, portal
mission-control remediate) sit behind requireAdmin / requireRole(...), which REJECT the ingest
token with 401 BEFORE the isTestbed check is ever reached. The headless harness cannot mint the
admin / MSPOperator / PlatformAdmin JWT those routes require (same credential boundary the
money-path-e2e manifest documents — no admin session is available here), so it cannot exercise
their in-handler isTestbed refusal directly. What #3-#7 DO assert, honestly, is that the write path
is unreachable at all with a non-admin credential — i.e. the AUTH WALL in front of each gate is
intact. Each sends a genuine breach payload (the same NON-testbed customerId, confirmed:true where
required) so that if anyone ever widens these routes to accept the ingest token (the prerequisite
for the harness to reach their gate) the observed status changes from 401 and the test fails loudly
— flagging that a real write endpoint just became reachable and its isTestbed gate now needs a
session-authenticated negative test of its own. This is NOT faked gate coverage: it is documented
as auth-wall coverage, per the test-coverage honesty rule.
The allow-path (a write against a genuine testbed tenant succeeding) is already exercised by
test-manifests/admin/baseline-actions-powershell-verify.json — this file is the deliberately-refused
counterpart, so together they prove the gate discriminates rather than blanket-refusing.
SHANE TO-DO: set BuildConsole Test Environment Variable NON_TESTBED_CUSTOMER_ID to a real, active,
connected, NON-testbed tenants.id before running; DEPLOY_URL + SECRET_KEY (= BUILD_TRACKER_INGEST_TOKEN)
as usual. Run against the real deploy.

apiTests.name: auth-proof: the ingest token genuinely authenticates to the testbed router — so a later refusal is provably the isTestbed gate, not an auth failure
REAL BREACH (the load-bearing test): authenticated ingest-token write against a NON-testbed tenant is refused by the isTestbed gate (baseline-templates/:templateId/test, requireAdminOrIngestToken)

containsAny: never point it at a live customer tenant

apiTests.name: breach attempt — write-actions PREVIEW against a NON-testbed tenant is refused before any write (requireAdmin auth wall in front of assertTestbedCustomer's 403; ingest token cannot reach the gate -> 401)
breach attempt — write-actions EXECUTE (confirmed:true) against a NON-testbed tenant is refused before any write (requireAdmin auth wall; ingest token -> 401, never reaches the 403 isTestbed gate)
breach attempt — Launch Control EXECUTE against a NON-testbed tenant is refused before any write (requireRole(MSPOperator) auth wall in front of the 403 isTestbed gate; ingest token -> 401)

breach attempt — Config Pack RUN against a NON-testbed tenant is refused before any write (requireRole(PlatformAdmin) auth wall in front of the orchestrator's customer_not_testbed -> 422 gate; ingest token -> 401)

breach attempt — Portal instant-remediation is refused for a non-session caller (requireRole + customerId derived from the caller's own token, so a foreign tenant can't even be targeted; ingest token -> 401, never reaches the 403 isTestbed gate)
